entries:
Alpha 1.17.0 (companions and the unmeasured sky)

  • Prepare together: the Dungeon Guide now shows advice for your selected dungeon and difficulty, your listed party and readiness, and direct routes to Party controls or activity-specific recruitment. Empty listings offer useful next steps. No automatic listing, invitation or run launch; all server entry gates remain.
  • Eight places in Air: observatory and weatherworks surrounds, the Tempest Spire muster, Horizon Orrery, courier and weatherkeeper camps, and two optional lore readings. New trails and atlas destinations share real positions; camps remain combat territory, not safe zones.
  • A quieter skyward ground: wind-scoured slate replaces the repeated glowing floor grid, with registered surface relief and roughness at both quality levels. New scenery keeps approaches clear and ordinary enemy spawn counts unchanged.
  • Inhabited Dark Realm streets: four meeting courts frame the existing witnesses and records. Ten worn streets and matching atlas routes connect the district circuit, witness approaches and Nexus threshold records. These are not replacement quest givers or new dungeon entrances.
  • Progress preserved: manual quest claims, rewards, level gates, party authority, latest-boss checkpoints and the 15-minute saved dungeon logout rule are unchanged. This is a population first pass, not final graphics or closed-beta certification; real-phone party and campaign pacing feedback remains with playtesting.
  • Full prior patch history: every earlier major and corrective release remains below.

Alpha 1.16.0 (tides, cinders and the way back)

  • Sixteen places across Water and Fire: Discover tide gauges, stranded boat ribs, sailcloth refuge, communal kilns, a workers’ court, cold furnaces and new landmarks. Existing story investigations and dungeon approaches receive distinct surroundings without changing their objectives or entry requirements.
  • Roads that match the map: Sixteen physical trails and branches connect these places, with detours around existing hazards and dungeon buildings. Atlas and minimap destinations use the same anchors; scenery clearings preserve sightlines. These routes and camps remain combat territory, not safe zones.
  • Four optional stories: Read the tidekeepers’ soundings, rescuers’ names, communal firing register and broken counterseal with ordinary interaction, E or mobile USE. Learn how care became control without receiving automatic quest credit, rewards or fabricated discovery ticks.
  • Quieter ground, clearer warnings: Water terrain now reads as frost-dusted rock; Fire terrain as cooled volcanic ground. Generated surface relief and roughness replace bright repeating ground cracks, leaving actual hazards distinct. High and Low retain matching physical patterns and collisions.
  • A usable way back: Failed session recovery returns to a visible login screen, clears the password and retires the old connection. Late socket/load callbacks cannot displace a newer session. Optional browser storage failures no longer prevent HUD construction or in-session settings changes. Login now includes connection and account-help guidance.
  • Preserved progress: Scenery blocks ordinary enemy spawns and unsafe administrator landings using shared geometry. Existing encounter counts, saved quests, rewards, combat balance, Gold/EP separation, dungeon checkpoints and the 15-minute logout rule remain unchanged. This is the Water/Fire population and account-continuity milestone, not final art or completed beta readiness. Earlier patch notes remain below.

Alpha 1.15.0 (roads, refuge and remembered promises)

  • A more inhabited Lanternhold: A communal well and menders’ yard add gathering spaces, work surfaces, resting benches and quietly working residents. These are scenery, not duplicate vendors; healing and Well Rested still work throughout the safe zone.
  • Reasons to explore Earth: Eight distinct locations dress the keeper’s abandoned home, crystal-root scar, Bastion approach, First Grove arch, pilgrim camp, foresters’ yard, bellkeeper’s cairn and oath stone. Connected physical trails also appear on the atlas. Solid scenery keeps clear approaches, and random enemy spawns avoid its footprints.
  • Stories beside the road: Inspect two optional readings with E or ordinary interaction/mobile USE to learn about shelter, broken trust and the grove’s promises. These readings are optional lore, not quests or reward sources, and do not pretend to be saved discoveries. Their windows close safely when you leave, die or change areas.
  • A map of real places: Places & lore destinations share world positions with the atlas and minimap, distinguish combat territory from town recovery, and guide Bastion gatherings outside the entrance. Existing story discovery visibility remains tied to your actual quest progress.
  • A clearer beginning: Class cards explain primary stats. Starting Your Journey covers Ilyra, manual quest claims, equipment, skill training, town recovery and exploration; phone guidance appears before the desktop keyboard reference.
  • Preserved progress: No changes to earned quests, reward amounts, combat balance, Gold/EP rules or the dungeon logout rule. This is the Lanternhold/Earth population milestone, not the completed world or final graphics overhaul; other realms follow next. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.14.0 (an atlas for the journey)

  • Find your next destination: A new searchable atlas has location details, category filters, readable marker shapes, a north compass and scale. Town services, real gate openings, dungeon entrances and portal requirements agree with the world. Cached terrain and forest cartography replaces the old checkerboard and level-band blocks.
  • Your route, your choice: Set and clear a personal waypoint with direction and straight-line distance on the map and minimap. Keyboard pan, mouse controls and touch pan/pinch work without moving or attacking underneath. Waypoints are guidance, not automatic movement, pathfinding or teleport access.
  • Follow your journal: Tracked quests show investigation sites, broad hunt areas, dungeon approaches and manual turn-ins. Gold story and blue daily markers distinguish available quests from ready rewards. Recorded discoveries follow your character’s saved records; hidden story text and prerequisite-locked discoveries stay hidden.
  • Know the space you are in: Dungeons and raids show their actual connected floors and current room guidance. Dark Realm, each casino floor and PvP have their own views. Party dots and waypoints respect instance/floor boundaries. Matching minimap icons and a facing indicator help you stay oriented.
  • Reports you can trust: The report form previews build/area context and optional bounded diagnostics. Sending keeps your draft until storage is acknowledged; offline, failure and uncertain replies do not silently discard it. No automatic chat, credential or character-state dumps are attached.
  • More world ahead: This is the first atlas and feedback milestone, not the completed populated-world or final graphics overhaul. New physical paths, settlements, camps and optional discoveries arrive in the following realm milestones. No quest rewards, combat balance, currencies or saved progress changed. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.13.0 (a lighter Lanternhold Casino)

  • Less invisible work: Characters and auras on the other casino floor no longer incur unnecessary scene-transform work. Hidden aura animations retain their elapsed time and catch up when you change floors.
  • The whole venue stays: Both full-sized floors, all 92 stations and 232 seats, equipped characters and visible effects remain intact. Streaming, floor changes and leaving the casino restore the current living characters without reviving removed bodies.
  • Same games and progression: No changes to wagers, payouts, Gold/EP rules, VIP access, equipment stats, quests or saved progress. This focused rendering update is not a universal device FPS guarantee or the later world/atlas overhaul. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.12.0 (the fourfold passage)

  • A real portal in Lanternhold: Find the Fourfold Resonance Portal in the southeast plaza, east of the Dungeon Guide and south of Ilyra. A stone arch, four elemental facets and a walkable inlaid circle make the passage a place in the world.
  • Your crystals, your passage: Dormant, resonance-ready and active presentation follows your own claimed repairs and level. Each traveler still needs level 100 and all four crystal-repair Vigils; an unlocked party leader cannot carry others in. Existing veteran access is preserved.
  • Follow the covenant: Ilyra directs you to the plaza after the final Vigil. Click the portal or approach and press E to see the four repairs, read its lore and choose to enter. The server rechecks your location and eligibility before sending you to the shared Resonant Foothold. The Dungeon Guide remains a fallback.
  • A clear way back: The portal explains Ilyra’s camp projection and Return to Lanternhold. Desktop and phone-sized dialogs support scrolling, keyboard focus and explicit entry; inspecting the portal never attacks it or grants a quest reward.
  • Places agree: Ilyra, the Guide and the portal now use a validated shared location registry for server placement and map markers. This is the foundation for the upcoming atlas and populated-world milestones, not the completed map overhaul.
  • Progress preserved: No reward, stat, currency, quest-contract or save-schema changes. Recall, private dungeon checkpoints and the 15-minute logout rule are unchanged. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.11.0 (Lanternhold takes shape)

  • Crafted town surfaces: Weathered masonry, layered slate courses and subtle timber grain replace flat building surfaces. Town and Earth ground now have generated normal/roughness detail, with cooler shadows against warm lanterns.
  • Leaves, not solid crowns: Ossuary birches have folded leaf geometry and varied color. Spatial rendering groups cull distant detailed trees without changing tree placement or collision.
  • Better-fitting shoulders: Steel and reinforced pauldrons use smaller hollow shells, overlapping plates and contrasting rims on the existing animated equipment anchors.
  • Casino maps match the venue: Maps use the expanded floor size, current-floor stations and guest markers, five distinct game symbols, correct guard/exit/stair positions and VIP access state. The upstairs minimap points downstairs instead of showing the public exit.
  • The road to beta: The 1.11–1.99 roadmap now includes meaningful populated locations, exploration activities and a world-map overhaul before closed beta. This release begins that visual work; it does not claim the complete world redesign or beta readiness.
  • Progress preserved: No changes to combat stats, rewards, currencies, saved quests or casino rules. The physical Dark Realm portal and remaining casino performance work are later milestones, not features shipped here. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.10.2 (Resilient administration history)

  • Recoverable read history: Administration status, online-player and history requests retain their audit entries during temporary audit-database outages, using the existing recovery journal.
  • Permissions stay strict: Failed audit writes still withhold privileged results. If both database and local storage fail, the connection closes and recovery remains pending; forced process loss can still lose entries held only in memory.
  • No gameplay changes: Combat, progression, rewards, saved characters, casino rules and currencies are unchanged. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.10.1 (Clearer victories)

  • Cleaner notifications: Story, victory and encounter notices no longer show an empty Attack power row. Normal enemy targeting restores its combat information.
  • Readable phone titles: Notification titles wrap instead of cutting off important words, in portrait and landscape. Ordinary enemy target cards remain compact.
  • Progress stays intact: No changes to rewards, combat stats, saved characters, currencies or the 15-minute dungeon logout rule.
  • Verification update: Group checks now cover all four elemental crystal-repair raids and the Umbral Nexus. A five-player Dark King victory and all five survivors' manual rewards, epilogues and relogin persistence are confirmed through the prepared encounter and its saved continuation. These checks use prepared parties and retained campaign progress; uninterrupted fresh-campaign and human pacing checks remain open. This is not exhaustive campaign sign-off. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.10.0 (The Resonant Age)

  • A complete world to playtest: The Fourfold Chronicle spans elemental investigations, dungeon clears, four defended crystal-repair raids and the level-100 Dark Realm expedition, Umbral Nexus and four-Eidolon Dark King finale. Ilyra's quests require explicit acceptance and manual turn-ins. Earlier releases' party, visual, mobile, casino and administration improvements are included.
  • A clearer leveling journey: New story offers provide preparation XP for the next area's enemies and dungeon entry. Repeatable combat and daily XP are balanced alongside those one-time rewards. The design targets are 2–3 hours to the first dungeon, roughly 100 hours to level 100, and another 8–12 hours in the Dark Realm; these are playtest targets, not measured guarantees.
  • Reachable long-term forging: Potency prices through +8 are unchanged. Later upgrades grow more gradually so every step through +20 can be paid from a normal inventory. +20 remains a long-term endgame investment, not expected story gear. Forge previews and server costs agree.
  • A tighter finale: New Dark King encounters have a smaller health pool to target a 5–10-minute five-player fight and bring the Eidolons' interventions into reach sooner. His damage, telegraphs and four phases are unchanged; party playtesting will guide further tuning.
  • Your progress stays yours: Existing levels, XP, Gold, gear and accepted reward quotes are preserved. Level-cap quest XP continues as Resonance XP. Town healing, Well Rested, latest-cleared-boss returns and the 15-minute dungeon logout rule remain in place. EP remains separate from Gold and cannot buy gameplay power.
  • Alpha playtest: Please report awkward controls, encounter difficulty and progression pacing. The latest five-player finale test reached phase III but did not clear the Dark King; raid acceptance remains open. Physical-phone party/dungeon feedback and comprehensive human campaign timing remain open; this release does not claim those measurements are complete. Full prior patch history is retained below.
